title: Check the workspace
goal: After writing records or code, an Agent checks the workspace, from the command line or through its tools, to find out whether the data is broken and what work is left, and fixes errors before handing the work back to the Owner.

title: Add a check
goal: The Owner decides on a new rule, and an Agent adds it as a check so that every later load enforces it.

title: Add a product's own checks
goal: A product has house rules that Lathe should not impose on every product. One product, for example, requires each aggregate to have exactly one use case that follows its Record view pattern, and this repo requires every operation to state at least one API requirement. Lathe ships no such rule. Instead the Owner, or an Agent, adds each rule as a check of the product, in the same form as Lathe's own checks, with Add a check from any of Lathe's interfaces; it lives in the product's data. The check run applies them after Lathe's checks and reports their problems with the others, so the product's rules live and change with the product.

title: Set the product's limits
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, keeps each level of a product's spec small enough to read and big enough to group something. `lathe check` warns when a record holds more children of one kind than the product's `max_children` setting (`product_setting`), when an aggregate holds more entities than its `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting, and when a group holds only one record, counting a flow's steps per path and requirements and rules per group, so that a missing or needless level, or an aggregate that is several, is found while the spec is written.

title: Review every problem of a product
goal: The owner looks at everything the checks found in one product, on its space's own Checks panel, with the problems that belong to no product, to see what is broken before reviewing an agent's work.

title: Report tests that count for nothing
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, runs `lathe check` and reads each pattern rule test whose domain does not owe its rule, with the reason, and each manual test whose file never mentions it.

title: Review the essential records with fresh eyes
goal: Before proposing a change to what a product is, an Agent reads the product's essential records alone, grouped by domain, as someone who knows the domain but not software would, and lists each record that person would not recognize or care about for the Owner to decide.

title: Make the product's check strict
goal: The Owner makes a product's check strict, accepting the warnings it has now, so that any warning beyond them and any gap fails the check as an error does, and the count of accepted warnings only moves down.

title: Set the product's technology words
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, gives a product the words, besides Lathe's own, that name technology in its essential records, so the check can tell a record that names how from one that says what; the first time adds the product's settings with the default limits.

title: Change a check
goal: The Owner changes a house rule of their product, and an Agent changes its check, so that the next check runs it as it is now; Lathe's own checks are read-only.

title: Remove a check
goal: The Owner removes a house rule of their product, and an Agent removes its check, so that the next check no longer runs it.

title: Find a record in a domain
goal: The reader opens a domain to find an invariant, a use case, a handler or a test, and to see what is missing. They read the product laid out in its stage folders, and a domain's technical specification and test plan by kind, from the nav, the domain page and the graph.

title: Open a record
goal: The reader reads one record and follows its links in either direction: from an obligation to the flow steps that fulfill it, the records that implement its design and the tests under it, or from a test back to its parent. To change a record the Owner edits it on its page (`LA-EXP-UC14`), or an Agent writes through the plugin; the page shows the change.

title: Walk the model as a graph
goal: The reader starts from any record, sees what it connects to, and walks the model as a graph by choosing one node after another. The graph is one map of the whole model that never changes shape: walking it is zooming in and out and centering. On a domain it reads like a folder tree, its stages and kind groups each a folder with its name, count and marks, so the shape of a domain and its traceability read at a glance.

title: Read a record
goal: The reader opens any record, group, domain or product at its one address and reads it two ways at once: its wiki page in the wiki card, and on the stage behind it among its neighbors (Graph), as an ERD, or as its traceability (Trace). Following a link in the card or a choice on the stage moves them both. They read a flow step by step and a domain's interface design, and find anything by ID or title.

title: Work in one product at a time
goal: The reader works on one product at a time, as in one workspace at a time in Slack, Discord, Linear or Notion. When the workspace shows two or more products, a rail at the far left of the nav shows each as a square icon; the reader chooses one and everything they see is that product's alone, as a separate space: the nav, quick find, its Checks, the wiki card, the graph and the ERD and Trace stages. They switch with Alt+1 to Alt+9 (⌥1 to ⌥9 on a Mac) or from the command palette, and come back to the page they left. With one product there is no rail, and the nav is that product's.

title: Open a new tab
goal: The Reader opens a record, a link or a found record in a new tab, as in a browser's tabs: a tab is a place, with its own focus, stage, camera, depth, kind filters, wiki card and its own Back and Forward. A new tab opens only when the Reader asks for one: Cmd or Ctrl with a selection, or a middle press, on a box or a link, Open in New Tab, Cmd+Enter in quick open, Cmd+T or Duplicate Tab. On the web the browser's own tabs are the tabs, each one place; in the app the tabs sit at the left of the page bar, and a reload brings them all back.

title: Fold or unfold a nav section
goal: The Reader folds or unfolds one of the nav's own sections, so the nav shows only what they are working in, and finds it as they left it at the next launch.

title: Cycle through the tabs
goal: The Reader cycles through the open tabs of a space with the keyboard, forward or back, wrapping around, instead of reaching for each tab strip entry.

title: Duplicate a tab
goal: The Reader wants a second look at a place without leaving it, so they duplicate its tab: the copy starts where the first stands, with its history and cameras, and takes over.

title: Resize the wiki card
goal: The Reader widens or narrows the wiki card over the stage to read more of a page or see more of the graph, or sets it back to its default width.

title: Resize the chat
goal: The Owner widens or narrows the chat panel beside the stage to give a long answer room or the stage more, or sets it back to its default width.

title: Turn Highlight changes on or off
goal: The Reader turns Highlight changes on to see what changed since their baseline marked on the pages and the stage, or off to read without the marks, for the browser session.

title: Choose the Changes baseline
goal: The Reader chooses what the Changes panel compares with: the last commit, the branch, or when they last looked, so it lists the changes they care about.

title: Note where a tab was
goal: The Reader scrolls the wiki card down a long page, follows a link and comes back, and finds the card where they left it: the tab notes where its page was in the history entry.

title: Review Claude's changes
goal: After Claude has changed the spec in the chat, the Owner sees what it changed on the stage: they put the turn's records under review, the stage lighting them alone while they step through each with its diff, and follow a record ID in its answer into a new tab. What they decide next is theirs: keep the change, or undo the turn (LA-PLT-UC27).
notes: It happens in the desktop app's chat (LA-PLT-UC19), after a turn that changed records.

title: Read a domain as an ERD
goal: The reader switches to the ERD stage on a domain and reads its domain model as an entity-relationship diagram: its aggregates as boundaries around their entities, and how their entities' reference fields join them. On an aggregate they read its entities with their fields and relationships, and on an entity the same diagram with that entity picked out. The diagram draws entities and their relationships only. They choose a box to go to it, and read the key at the foot of the diagram for the boxes and the lines.

title: Look up a record's history
goal: The Reader wants to know how a record came to be as it is, without leaving the page. At the end of the expanded wiki card a History section, read only when they ask for it, lists the commits that changed the record's data, the changes not committed yet first, each with what it changed.

title: Watch the spec change
goal: As the product's data changes, by the Reader, by an Agent through any of Lathe's interfaces, or by a git pull, the Reader sees it on the stage in real time: live marks on the records added, changed and removed, Highlight changes, which makes every change obvious against a baseline (a New, Changed or Removed pill on each changed record, everything unchanged dimmed, a roll-up on every container, markers and hints for changes out of view), Next change and Previous change to walk them, the diff in the wiki card, a Changes panel listing the changes, and Follow, which glides the camera to each change as it lands.

title: Choose the graph's layout
goal: The reader chooses the graph's layout (Tree, Nested or Map) for the rest of the session, whatever page they are on and however they move.

title: Fold or unfold a nav entry
goal: The Reader folds an entry of the nav away, or unfolds it, so the part of the product they are reading stays in view and the rest is out of the way.

title: Turn Follow on or off
goal: The Reader turns Follow on so the camera glides to each change as it lands, and off again, so they can read a change in their own time.

title: Show or hide the minimap
goal: The Reader shows the graph's minimap to see the whole map at a glance, or hides it to leave the stage clear, and the choice lasts the session.

title: Show or hide all links
goal: The Reader has the Map draw every link between the records in view, or only the focus's, and the choice lasts the session.

title: Activate a tab
goal: The Reader flips between the places they have open, and the address follows the one in front.

title: Change a tab's view
goal: The Reader sets the depth, the kind filters and the wiki card of the place they are on, and each tab keeps its own.

title: Go back or forward in a tab
goal: The Reader goes Back and Forward through the places the active tab has been, never into another tab's history.

title: Close a tab
goal: The Reader closes a tab they have finished with, and the one beside it comes forward.

goal: The Owner, or an Agent, renames a domain the check finds named for a technology.

title: Move a term to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a glossary term to the domain whose language it is.

title: Move a repository to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a repository to the domain of the aggregate it persists.

title: Move a domain service to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a domain service, with its service and tests, to another domain.

title: Add an entity
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a child entity with its fields, linked from the root by has_one or has_many, another aggregate referenced by a typed field.

title: Add an invariant
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the aggregate's invariants, a uniqueness rule named on its unique key.

title: Move an aggregate to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves an aggregate, with everything under it, to another domain.

title: Add a command handler
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the command's handler, naming its file.

title: Add a policy
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a policy under the command it invokes, hearing one event and naming the integrations it exchanges with, with its test.

title: Add a specification test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the specification's test.

title: Remove a specification
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a specification nothing checks or selects by.

title: Move a specification to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a specification, with its predicate and test, to another domain.

title: Add a query
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds each query under the read model it reads, with its handler.

title: Add a projection
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the projection that builds the read model.

title: Add a reader
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the reader the query handlers read the read model through.

title: Move a read model to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a read model, with its queries, projection and reader, to another domain.

title: Add a constraint
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the value object's constraints, each with its test.

title: Remove a value object
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a value object no field is typed by.

title: Add an event type
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the event's type, delivered by outbox when a policy hears it.

title: Change a domain event
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, marks the event published when other domains hear it.

title: Add a storage requirement test
goal: They add its storage requirement test.

title: Change a storage requirement
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes the storage requirement's statement.

title: Change a storage requirement test
goal: They change its storage requirement test's state and file.

title: Remove a storage requirement test
goal: They remove a storage requirement test.

title: Remove a storage requirement
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes the storage requirement whole, told that its tests go with it.

title: Load the workspace
goal: Code such as the server's kept checks' run, or an agent's script, calls `loadWorkspace(root)` to get every record, link, problem and coverage figure for the repo at `root`.

title: Set up Lathe in a product repo
goal: Lathe is installed into a product's own repo as a package, so the product's data files live beside its code and Lathe's improvements arrive with a version bump instead of by copying. The Owner runs lathe init, sets up the merge driver once per clone, and lists the workspace's other products in its config; lathe check then reads each product's records from the data folder its config names.

title: See the current data
goal: While an Agent changes records with the aggregates' commands, the Reader keeps the browser open and expects it to show what is in the data files now, reloaded on the file watcher's Data files changed, and to say what is wrong when the data cannot be loaded.

title: Resize a panel
goal: The reader sizes the navigation and the wiki card floating over the stage to suit what they are reading, as in VS Code: they drag a panel's edge, or focus it and use the keyboard, and the stage frames the focus again in what is left. Lathe remembers the sizes, and a quick double press on an edge resets one.

title: Choose a theme
goal: The reader picks how Lathe looks, as in VS Code: one of a few built-in themes (Lathe, High contrast, Workshop, Midnight and Graphite), arrowing through them to see each at once, or from Appearance in the nav's footer, which shows every theme with a preview.

title: Show a record's menu
goal: From a record, the Reader opens a menu of what they can do with it: open it in a new tab, reveal its data file, open it in the editor or copy its ID.

title: Reveal a product folder
goal: When a product's folder will not open, or the Reader wants it in Finder, they reveal it in the system file manager from the window's launch or error view.

title: Read a product's changed data files again
goal: The Owner changes a product's data files in an editor, by a merge or a checkout, and expects every window to read again only the files that changed and show what they now hold, or say what is wrong with them.

title: Merge two branches' data
goal: Two branches each change a product's data, an Agent's and the Owner's. When git merges them, the merge driver merges each data file record by record against the base, keeps both sides' records, sorts them again and checks the table's own rules, so that only a real clash stops the merge: one key added on both sides with different content, or one record changed on both sides.

title: Open a product in a window
goal: The reader opens a product's folder, such as Lathe's own repo or another product's, and it opens in a window of its own with the product's name and folder in the title bar. Lathe in that window reads and live-reloads that folder, as in the browser. They come back to it from File › Open Recent, and the shell reopens the last folder when it starts.

title: Start Lathe with hot reload
goal: The owner changes Lathe while using it in its own window. npm --prefix desktop run dev loads the Workbench with hot reload: from the owner's own dev server on port 5199 when it serves the opened folder, so the browser and the shell share it, or from a dev server of the shell's own. Changing the shell itself restarts it, and record changes reload the view in every mode. When they want Lathe as it ships, they build it locally, unsigned.

title: Upgrade a product's data
goal: A product repo outside Lathe's own moves to a new Lathe safely: a Lathe reads only data for its own schema version, and lathe upgrade converts a product's data forward, one way, as one reviewable commit, listing what it could not convert. The Product window (LA-PLT-UC11) and the plugin (LA-PLT-UC18) use the product's own installed Lathe.

title: Start the plugin's tools in a product repo
goal: An Agent works on a product repo in Claude Code with Lathe's plugin. The plugin's launcher finds the repo and the Lathe installed in it and starts that Lathe's tools for the Agent, so the Agent writes through the product's own Lathe; when the plugin's skills were written for another major version of Lathe, the first tool result says so once, and the Agent knows its skills may not match the tools.

title: Send a message to Claude
goal: The Owner works with Claude inside Lathe: in the chat panel beside the stage their own Claude Code runs in the product folder, with their login, settings, skills, plugins, tool servers and CLAUDE.md. They send it a message in their own words, with what they are looking at as context. Claude's answers read as rich text whose record IDs open the record on the stage, its tool calls are compact entries that expand, and the records it changed show as diffs.
notes: Runs the user's own `claude` CLI headless with structured input and output (`-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio`, with `--resume <id>` and `--fork-session`); there is no API-key path and no agent loop of Lathe's own. Desktop only: the web app and a phone have no chat. Not yet: the CLI's interactive extras (slash-command dialogs, plan-mode approval, question cards); slash commands go to the CLI as text, and the panel's help lists what is not supported.

title: Listen for a dictated message
goal: The Owner talks to the desktop chat instead of typing: they dictate a message, its words appearing in the message box as they speak, and edit and send it. Speech is recognized on the Mac itself: no audio leaves it, and nothing is recorded or saved. How the chat listens, by a wake phrase and with Quick mode, is the Owner's choice (LA-PLT-UC26).
notes: macOS 26 or later only; elsewhere the mic is hidden. Words are recognized by NVIDIA's Parakeet model on the Mac (fetched once, about 0.6 GB, the first time the Owner dictates), or by macOS's SpeechAnalyzer when that model cannot be loaded. It happens in the desktop app's chat (LA-PLT-UC19).

title: Capture the stage
goal: The Owner sends Claude the stage as it is drawn, as an image with their message, or pastes an image, and types a slash for a skill or command, each with its one-line description.
notes: It happens in the desktop app's chat (LA-PLT-UC19); speaking a message is LA-PLT-UC20.

title: Serve the spec from a product repo
goal: The Owner runs lathe serve in a product repo to browse and edit its spec in the Workbench, with no build tools in the repo: every product the workspace lists shows as its own space, each change is written to its own product's folder, and stopping the server from the terminal leaves no storage work running.

title: Bind a key
goal: The reader gives a shortcut the keys they want: in the shortcuts sheet they bind a new key, and every hint follows at once: the palette, the sheet, the tooltips, what assistive technology announces and, in a Product window, the menus.

title: Open a record's data file in the editor
goal: From a record, the Owner opens the data file that holds it in the editor they chose, from the wiki card or the record's context menu; the shell takes only the record's ID and finds the file itself.

title: Choose the voice phrases
goal: The Owner chooses the wake phrase and the commands' words the desktop chat listens for: after a pause, while its window is in front, the wake phrase wakes the chat, and spoken commands send, clear or edit the draft. Speech is recognized on the Mac itself.
notes: macOS 26 or later only; elsewhere the Voice menu is hidden. It happens in the desktop app's chat (LA-PLT-UC19).

title: Undo Claude's turn
goal: After Claude has changed the spec in the chat, the Owner undoes the whole turn in one step, which puts the records back through their aggregates' own commands, or is told why it cannot be undone.
notes: It happens in the desktop app's chat (LA-PLT-UC19), after a turn that changed records, usually once the Owner has reviewed it (LA-EXP-UC109).

title: Clear the recent folders
goal: The reader clears the folders the app remembers having opened, from File › Open Recent, so neither the menu nor the Dock lists them any longer.

title: Open a record for the Owner
goal: While the Owner works with it, the Agent asks what the Owner is looking at in their window (the focused record and the stage) and opens a record there for them to see, through its app tools or Lathe's commands, and is refused when no window is connected.

title: Sign the agent in
goal: When the chat's agent is not signed in, the Owner signs it in from inside the product with their own account, never in a terminal: the product finds the agent signed out before a conversation starts or when a turn says so, starts the agent's own sign-in, which finishes in the browser, and passes on what the sign-in asks for.
notes: The agent is the Owner's own Claude Code (LA-PLT-UC19): the product runs its `claude auth login` (`--claudeai` for a Claude subscription, `--console` for a Console account) with no terminal, `claude auth status --json` to learn whether it is signed in, and `claude auth logout`. The product never reads, keeps or logs a credential, nor puts one on a command line: it keeps only the sign-in page's link the CLI prints, whether it asks for a code, and its last line when it fails. One sign-in serves the whole app, as the agent keeps one for every folder.

title: Show or hide a panel
goal: The Reader folds a panel away, or brings it back, and the stage takes the room, so the workbench shows only what they are reading.

title: Choose a color mode
goal: The Reader switches Light, Dark or System, which decides which of every theme's two color sets shows.

title: Duplicate a theme
goal: The Reader copies the theme closest to what they want, to edit the copy.

title: Edit a theme
goal: The Reader changes the colors, fonts and density of a theme of their own, with the app changing around them.

title: Export a theme
goal: The Reader exports a theme as a file, to share it with someone else.

title: Reset a theme
goal: The Reader puts their copy back to the theme it came from.

title: Delete a theme
goal: The Reader deletes a theme of their own they no longer want, after being asked.

title: Import a theme file
goal: The Reader adds a theme file someone shared as a theme of their own.

title: Turn scroll to zoom on or off
goal: The Reader has scroll zoom the stage, or pan it, as they prefer.

title: Save a window's place
goal: The Reader moves or resizes a window, and its size and place are kept, so the folder opens there next time.

title: Close a product window
goal: The Reader closes a product window, its place is kept, and its server and chat stop.

title: Stop Claude's turn
goal: The Owner stops the turn Claude has under way, and the chat waits for their next message.

title: Answer a permission prompt
goal: The Owner answers the prompt a tool waits at: allow it once, allow it always in this chat, or deny it.

title: Open a Claude Code session
goal: The Owner starts the chat on a new session, resumes a saved one or forks the one open elsewhere, with Lathe's tools loaded.

title: Choose the chat's permission mode
goal: The Owner chooses what Claude may do without asking, from Ask to View only, and the folder keeps the choice.

title: Choose the chat's model and effort
goal: The Owner chooses the model and the effort Claude works at, from the chat's head.

title: Take a message out of the queue
goal: The Owner sends more messages while Claude works, and takes one out of the queue before it goes.

title: Remove a binding
goal: The Reader takes a key they no longer want off a shortcut, in the shortcuts sheet.

title: Reset a shortcut
goal: The Reader puts a changed shortcut back to its own keys.

title: Reset all shortcuts
goal: The Reader puts every shortcut back to its own keys, after the sheet asks first.

title: Reveal a record's data file
goal: The Owner shows the data file that holds a record in the system file manager.

title: Copy a record's ID
goal: The Owner copies a record's ID to the clipboard, to name the record elsewhere.

title: Choose an editor
goal: The Owner chooses the editor Open in editor uses, or a command of their own, and the shell keeps it in its settings file.

title: Open the settings file
goal: The Owner opens the shell's settings file in the editor, to fill in a custom editor command.

title: Turn voice activation on or off
goal: The Owner has the chat listen for its wake phrase while the window is in front, or stop.

title: Turn Quick mode on or off
goal: The Owner has a dictated message sent by itself when they have finished, or not.

title: Give the sign-in code
goal: The Owner gives the code the browser showed to the sign-in under way, which asked for it.

title: Cancel the sign-in
goal: The Owner cancels the sign-in under way, which leaves everything as it was.

title: Sign the agent out
goal: The Owner signs the agent out of its account, so another can sign in.

title: Declare a product kind
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, declares a product kind with its fields, in a stage.

title: Add a product
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a product, the root of a set of specifications, with its title, its description and the roles its records name.

title: Change a product kind
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a product kind they declared: its label, description, parent kind, stage, obligation, ID pattern, example or title form, or its fields, as the product's own records need.

title: Remove a product kind
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a kind the product declared and no longer uses, with its fields.

title: Change a product relation
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes how a relation of the product's own reads between a pair of kinds: its role, its labels or its description.

title: Remove a product relation
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a pair of kinds a relation of the product's own may link, once no link of the pair is left.

title: Change an open question
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes an open question: its title, the role that decides it, its description, or the records it is about.

title: Remove an interface
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes an interface of a product, with its roles and the use cases it offers, once nothing else depends on it.

title: Remove a business outcome
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a business outcome the product no longer exists to bring about, with the links to what measures it.

title: Change a journey
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a journey: its title, its trigger, its result or its notes, or the business outcomes it serves.

title: Read the reference generated from the schema
goal: The owner, or an agent, reads how every kind, table, field, relation, stage and check works without opening the migrations or the checks: the reference script writes it from the schema and the checks, with a product's own kinds and checks, into `lathe/REFERENCE.md`, saying what clean architecture's use case is in Lathe (a command handler), and the API serves the same reference. Nothing in it is written by hand, so a new kind or check needs no edit, and the store refuses a product kind, relation or check that the reference would leave blank.

title: Remove a journey
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a journey whole, with its steps and its test, never the use cases and policies its steps carry out.

title: Remove a journey step
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a step of a journey, with the link to the use case or policy it carried out.

title: Change a journey test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a journey's test: how it runs, its steps and expected result, or the test data it starts from.

title: Remove a journey test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a journey's test, with the links it starts.

title: Look up an entry in the reference
goal: The Reader meets a kind or a check while reading the spec (a record's kind in the wiki card, a problem's code, a field) and opens what the reference says about it in one step, without leaving the workbench. Each kind and each check has its own entry, built from the schema and the checks, so it is never out of date: a kind's stage, fields, links and checks with a real example from the product, and a check's explanation and query with the problems it reports now. The record format's own entry says how records are kept and indexes everything.

title: Follow a journey step by step
goal: The Reader opens a journey and reads its steps in order, a list per path, the main path first: what happens at each, the use case or handoff it carries out, who acts and in which domain, with the aggregate or read model of its result. They follow a step to its use case or policy, and from a use case or policy back to the journeys it is a step of, with the steps before and after it; in the graph the steps sit under their journey, in order.

title: Add a business outcome
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds each business outcome under the product, with its statement, measure and target.

title: Add an interface
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds each interface of the product, of its kind, with the roles that use it and the use cases it offers.

title: Add a journey
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the journey under the product, with its trigger, its result and the outcomes it serves.

title: Add an extension record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a record of the product's own kind under its parent, with the fields and links its kind declares.

title: Change a product's roles
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, names the roles of the product (A1), the parts people and agents play that its use cases name as actors (Lathe's are Owner, Reader and Agent), each with what it does, through the Product aggregate's commands, which hold the product to its rules.

title: Add an open question
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds an open question under the product or a domain, with the role that decides it and the records it concerns.

title: Declare a product relation
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, declares product relations, new or adding a pair to Lathe's.

title: Change a business outcome
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, links each outcome to the tests or records that measure it, or says how it is measured outside the code.

title: Change an interface
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes an interface's description, roles or the use cases it offers.

title: Add a journey step
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds its steps in order, the main path first, then each alternate path, each carrying out a use case, a policy as a handoff, or nothing yet.

title: Move a journey step
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a step to another place on its path, or to another path.

title: Change a journey step
goal: Once a step's use case is written, the Owner links the step to it.

title: Add a journey test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the journey test, its main path end to end.

title: Change an extension record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes the record's fields or links.

title: Remove an extension record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes the record with its links.

title: Move an extension record to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a record of the product's own kind to another domain.

title: Move an open question
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a question between the product and its domains, to where it belongs.

title: Remove an open question
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a decided question once its answer is in the records it affects.

title: Remove an entry point
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes an entry point of a domain, with the packages and helper files it names, once nothing references it.

title: Remove a tooling record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a tooling record of a domain, with the packages and helper files it names, once nothing references it.

title: Change a standard
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a standard's title or description.

title: Remove a standard
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a standard whole, with its rules and their tests.

title: Add a standard rule
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a rule to a standard, stated with MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY.

title: Remove a standard rule
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a rule of a standard, with its tests, once no record meets it.

title: Change a standard rule test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a standard rule's test: how it runs, or the test data it starts from.

title: Remove a standard rule test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a standard rule's test, with the links it starts.

title: Remove a table
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a table whole, with its keys and the links, packages and helper files it names, once nothing else references it.

title: Add a standard
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a standard and its rules.

title: Add a table
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a table under the entity, read model or domain it stores, with its storage, the data store it is kept in and the file that creates it.

title: Add an entry point
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds an entry point under its domain, titled as in code, naming the file that starts it.

title: Add a tooling record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a tooling record under its domain, titled as in code, naming its script or configuration.

title: Add a data store
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a data store under it, for the repositories, readers and tables kept there to name.

title: Add a standard rule test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds each rule's standard rule tests.

title: Change a standard rule
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a rule's statement when the standard proves wrong.

title: Change a table
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a table's keys, a unique key naming the invariant it enforces.

title: Move a table
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a table to the record it now stores.

title: Change an entry point
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes an entry point's file when it moves.

title: Move an entry point to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves an entry point to another domain.

title: Change a tooling record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a tooling record's file when it moves.

title: Move a tooling to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a tooling record to another domain.

title: Change a data store
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes the data store's kind or description.

title: Remove a data store
goal: They remove a data store nothing is kept in.

title: Move a data store to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a data store of one domain to another domain.

title: See how complete each domain is
goal: The Owner, or the Reader, asks how complete a product's domains are: for each domain, how many of its obligations (constraints, invariants, specifications, policies, domain services, UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and any obligation kind the product declares) are designed, built and proved, how many have only a test not automated yet, and which ones are not done. The Owner runs lathe check; the Reader opens the product in the app, with its summary, open questions and problems beside the domains. LA-TRC-UC02 says how each is decided.

title: Check that each test's file names it
goal: A test says what it proves by where it sits. A person, or an AI agent, writes the test and its code, and `lathe check` confirms that the code names the test, so each test record leads to the code that runs it.
notes: The person fixes each error by naming the test's ID in the test's name. A test whose file does not name it proves nothing: its obligation stays not proved, in the warnings and in coverage alike.

title: See each domain's tests by state
goal: The Owner, an Agent or the Reader learns how many tests each domain has by state, automated, manual and not automated yet, beside its coverage, as a real product's test-coverage summary counts them: the Owner from lathe check, an Agent from its machine-readable output, the Reader in the app beside each domain's coverage, with the product's total in its summary.

title: Follow a pattern
goal: A real product adopts most of its patterns for a whole domain, writes several with no settings, and asks only for proof of their rules. The Owner, or an Agent, links a domain to a pattern with follows, and gives a pattern no settings where it has none. Coverage then counts each rule in that domain, as it does for a domain whose use cases follow the pattern, and asks only for proof. A use case that follows a pattern needs no requirements of its own. A product's own kind may be declared an obligation.

title: Trace obligations from design to tests
goal: The Reader switches to the Trace stage and reads each use case of the product as one line, left to right: the business outcomes its aggregate or read model serves, the use case, its flow, its technical flow and its acceptance test suite, each stage with how far it has come (designed, built, proved). They open a line's stages down to its requirements, flows, steps, technical chain and tests, and select a requirement to light its path across the line, from the steps that fulfill it to the tests that prove it. Gaps show at once.

title: Stop following a pattern
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, ends a domain's or a use case's following of a pattern, with the setting values it gave it, because the pattern no longer describes how it is done.

title: Stop filling a slot
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, ends a technical record's fill of a slot, because the record no longer stands in for what the pattern could not say.

title: Remove a provider
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes the provider of a record, because it is no longer provided from outside the product.

title: See coverage of every obligation kind
goal: The Reader reads coverage for every kind of obligation the model names (UC requirements, view and API requirements, the domain model's rules and any kind the product adds), finds each view or API requirement under its view or operation, and tells at a glance which tests are automated, which are manual and which are not automated yet.

title: See a domain's owed pattern rules
goal: The Reader opens a domain and sees which patterns its use cases follow, and for each pattern rule, all of which the domain owes, whether the domain proves it, as a real product's "Patterns we follow" lists do. They open a pattern to see its settings, its rules and who follows it.

title: Trace an obligation to its proof
goal: The Reader opens an obligation and, below its text, reads its Traceability: its chain as the engine works it out (what designs it, what builds it, each marked built or not, and the tests under it, each with its state), with a callout for each gap coverage finds. A use case's Traceability shows its requirements by Designed, Built and Proved; a technical record's, the obligations it builds and their tests; a test's, what it proves and its run by. Every list is titled by its links' label. It is how someone new to a product finds the code and the tests behind a requirement they are given (LA-BO10).

title: Check that addresses match the code both ways
goal: An operation or a view says where it is served by its address. A person, or an AI agent, writes the record and the code that serves it, and lathe check confirms both ways that they agree: the code of what implements each record names its address, and every address the code serves has a record. An address changed on one side and not the other, or served with no record, is found.
notes: The code is read as text, not run: an address built at run time, matched by a prefix, kept in a configuration file or given by a framework's file layout is not recognized as served. Name such an address in a comment of the file that serves it.

title: Check each stored record kind against the file that creates it
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, writes each kind of record kept in its own storage with the file that creates it: a migration, a schema or the code that makes it. lathe check reads that file and confirms it defines the stored kind as the spec says, by its name, its fields and its keys, so the spec and the real schema cannot drift apart unseen.
notes: The file is read as text, never run. What it recognizes, and what it does not compare, is in the check's explanation.

title: Account for every package the product depends on
goal: Every package a product's manifests list is there for a reason the spec names: a connector that calls it, an interface part that renders with it, a tooling record that runs it. lathe check reads the manifests and reports each package no technical record names, so a dependency never enters unexplained, and reports a record that names a package no manifest lists, so the claim never outlives the dependency.
notes: It reads each manifest as structured data, the four sections of package names alike: a dev dependency is tooling the product runs, so it is accounted for as a runtime one is. It does not read lock files, workspaces or other ecosystems' manifests, and it does not judge whether code imports a package: knip finds a dependency no code uses.

title: See the outcomes each record serves
goal: The Reader, or an Agent, opens any record and learns which business outcomes it serves, without anyone having typed the link in: the use cases that reach it say so. What no outcome reaches is reported, so it can be given the use case that needs it or removed.

title: Fill a slot by hand
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, records that a technical record written by hand fills a slot of the pattern it is owed to, so the accidental complexity it holds is accounted for as debt at that slot until the pattern can express it. A record decided outside the product names its provider instead (LA-TRC-UC23). An engineering standard fills no slot: the records that meet its rules account for it.

title: See how far each journey is proved
goal: The Reader, or an Agent, reads for each journey of a product how far it is proved: its steps, how many carry out nothing yet, how many are proved (a use case's requirements and flow test, a handoff's policy test) and whether its journey test counts; with the journey itself, with each outcome it serves, and in the product's trace, where the journeys sit between the outcomes and the use cases.

title: Name what provides a record
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, names what provides a record decided outside the product, such as the outside service that keeps its data or the platform it runs on, so coverage counts it as accounted for rather than as hand-written debt.

title: See what a change would touch
goal: Before a change is made, the Owner names the records they mean to change and reads everything the change would touch: the records that name them or build on them, down to the code that implements them and the tests that prove them, and up to the use cases, journeys and business outcomes they serve. The Owner narrows the change until it touches only what they mean it to, so any break it makes is one they chose; an Agent reads the same reach before it changes anything.
notes: It is how a change breaks nothing by accident (LA-BO11): the Owner knows what a change breaks before it is made, and the break is deliberate. Coverage and a record's Traceability (LA-TRC-UC14) read one record's chain; this reads the reach of a whole change, in both directions, before it happens.

title: Change the setting values
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, gives the settings of a pattern their values for a domain or use case that already follows it, or none where the pattern has none.

title: Add a test data set
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a test data set under its domain, with the file that builds it.

title: Change a test data set
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a data set's preparation and reset.

title: Remove a test data set
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a data set no test starts from.

title: Move a test data set to another domain
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a test data set to the domain whose tests start from it.

title: Add a use case test
goal: A person writes each test under the one record it proves, of the test kind for that record, and says how it runs in its run by: a level (unit, integration, service, system or browser, the lowest that can observe its result), a state (automated, manual or not automated yet), and a file, or for a manual test the reason it is manual. The store refuses a run by that breaks these rules; `lathe check` reports a test whose file is missing or does not name it.
notes: The store refuses a test without a state, or an automated test without a file; `lathe check` reports a test whose file is missing or does not back what it proves.

title: Add a pattern rule test
goal: A pattern states behavior that several use cases share. Its rules are written once, as `pattern_rule` records under the pattern. Every domain that follows the pattern (the domain itself or one of its use cases `follows` it) owes every rule and must prove each in a pattern rule test of its own, naming the domain: proof in one domain says nothing about another. Pattern rules need proof only. A rule that holds for only some followers is not a pattern rule: it belongs to those use cases as their own requirement.
notes: The person writes the rules under the pattern, writes one pattern rule test per rule in each following domain, naming that domain, and runs `lathe check`. Coverage shows one pattern rule line per domain; the gaps and the `not-proved` warnings name the rule and the domain that still owes it. The store refuses a second test of one rule in one domain; a pattern nobody follows is reported.

title: Add a pattern
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a pattern with its settings.
notes: Lathe checks only how patterns are used, not house rules about them: a rule such as "each aggregate has exactly one use case following its Record view pattern" is the product's own check (LA-CHK-UC05).

title: Add a use case
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds a use case with its actors and requirements, in groups where a long list needs them.

title: Add a pattern rule
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds each of its rules, and a pattern rule test per following domain.

title: Change a pattern rule
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, changes a rule's statement.

title: Add a flow
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds its one flow, its ID the use case's and FL.

title: Add a flow step
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the flow's steps in order on their paths, each with what it fulfills and invokes, and the interface it is a variant of when only one does it.

title: Change a use case
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a use case so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a use case's title, goal, result or notes, or its actors (the whole list, in order). Its domain changes only by Move a use case.

title: Add a UC requirement
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to add a UC requirement so that the spec stays true to the product. The command adds a UC requirement to its use case.

title: Change a UC requirement
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a UC requirement so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a UC requirement's title, statement or group.

title: Remove a UC requirement
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a UC requirement so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a UC requirement with its use case tests and the links they start. Refused while a step fulfills it, or anything else references it or its tests.

title: Change a flow
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a flow so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a flow's title, which is its use case's.

title: Change a flow step
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a flow step so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a step's title or the interface it is a variant of (null makes it every interface's), or its links: a list given replaces the list, null clears what it invokes. Its path and position change only by Move a flow step.

title: Remove a flow step
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a flow step so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a flow step with the links it starts. Refused while anything else references it.

title: Remove a use case test
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a use case test so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a use case test with the links it starts. Refused while anything else references it, such as a business outcome it measures.

title: Change a flow test
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a flow test so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a flow test's way of running or the test data sets it starts from (the whole list).

title: Add a flow test
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, adds the use case tests and the flow test, its acceptance test.

title: Remove a flow test
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a flow test so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a flow test with the links it starts. Refused while anything else references it, such as a business outcome it measures.

title: Change a pattern
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a pattern so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a pattern's title, description or notes, or its settings (the whole list, in order). Its product never changes.

title: Remove a pattern
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a pattern so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a pattern whole: its settings, rules and rule tests, and the links they start. Refused while anything outside it references what is in it, such as a follower.

title: Remove a pattern rule
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a pattern rule so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a pattern rule with its tests and the links they start. Refused while anything references it or them.

title: Change a pattern rule test
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a pattern rule test so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a pattern rule test's way of running, the domain it proves the rule in, or the test data sets it starts from (the whole list).

title: Remove a pattern rule test
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a pattern rule test so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a pattern rule test and the links it starts. Refused while anything references it.

title: Add a slot
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to add a slot so that the spec stays true to the product. The command adds a slot to its pattern: an open-ended part code fills against its contract, with the reason its fills vary by design when they do.

title: Change a slot
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to change a slot so that the spec stays true to the product. The command changes a slot's title or contract, or the reason its fills vary by design; null clears the reason. Its pattern does not change.

title: Remove a slot
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to remove a slot so that the spec stays true to the product. The command removes a slot from its pattern. Refused while a record fills it.

title: Move a flow step
goal: An Agent, or the Owner, needs to move a flow step so that the spec stays true to the product. The command moves a step to another position, on its own path or another, shifting the steps of the old path and the new so each stays numbered 1, 2, 3.

title: Remove a flow
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, removes a flow with its steps and test.

title: Move a use case
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a use case, with everything in it, to another domain, with a result of that domain.

title: Move a UC requirement to another use case
goal: The Owner, or an Agent, moves a UC requirement, with its tests, to the use case whose goal it serves.

title: Change a use case test
goal: A person changes how a test is run, its level, state, file, size or markers, so that every rule of its run by still holds.

title: Remove a use case
goal: Removing a use case a step carries out is refused, naming the step.
